subject: Post-call: SignalWave latency/throughput deep-dive & mutual next steps
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Patel <asha.p@signalwave.ai>, Luke Morgan <luke.morgan@signalwave.ai>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Mar 2028 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: SignalWave latency/throughput deep-dive & mutual next steps

Hi Asha & Luke —

Thanks for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from my side so we have a single reference:

Call summary (30m)
- Pain: production NLU service is seeing 150–250ms p95 today at ~60 QPS; batch spikes push up to 500ms. Token costs and tail latency are the top blockers for pushing more features.
- Goal: get to a stable 100–150ms p95 at 100–150 sustained QPS for interactive endpoints, with a plan for burst capacity up to 400 QPS.
- Model: you mentioned a medium-sized LLM (approx 13B) for embeddings + summarization, and a smaller 3–7B for routing/priors.

Technical constraints you called out
- Strict P95 latency target for user-facing prompts (100–150ms)
- KV cache must persist between short sessions (30–120s) and be local to reduce tokens served
- Data residency: US only for now, SOC2 required for enterprise features

Attachments: I’ve attached a starter SLO matrix (signalwave-slo-matrix.xlsx) and a short Redwood quickstart (redwood-quickstart.pdf) — these are draft templates to align on numbers.

Proposed next steps (customer/internal owners)
1) You: share 24–72h baseline metrics (p50/p95/p99, QPS distribution, token counts, tail spikes) and current infra topology. (Asha) — due Thu 2028-03-22
2) Us: produce two topology sketches (hosted + dedicated-pool hybrid) with rough cost/backfill and a short canary plan. (Aditya / Marcus) — draft by Tue 2028-03-26
3) Technical deep-dive call (60m) with your SRE + our infra team to validate KV/cache behavior and routing policy. (Irene to join) — propose Wed 2028-03-28 or Thu 2028-03-29

Open questions for SignalWave
- Can you share an example request distribution (percent interactive vs batch) and average conversation length?
- Do you currently encrypt KV cache at rest or is that an operational gap?

If that aligns, I’ll draft the topology sketches and a mutual action plan.

Thanks again — short actions are easiest to track.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Solutions | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call: SignalWave latency/throughput deep-dive & mutual next steps

Thanks Aditya — this looks great and aligned with what we discussed. A few clarifications from my side: 

- Baseline metrics: attaching a short snapshot (sample_metrics.txt) — note these are from our staging cluster; prod will show similar tails. Our typical interactive traffic is ~70% of requests; batch jobs run nightly and account for high token churn but are queueable.
- KV: we currently persist a per-instance in-memory cache backed by Redis (single-region). We do not encrypt the cached values today — can discuss compliance implications.
- Models: confirmed: 13B LLM for primary generation, 6B for routing/heuristics. Model weights live on S3 (us-east-1).

Actions on our side:
- I’ll get the 72h prod metrics and a short topology sketch to you by Thu (22 Mar).
- Please include an estimate for a dedicated-reserved pool vs hosted (we need ballpark cost to take to procurement).

Also — can you share a topology diagram that shows where Redwood would sit relative to our SRE stack and our Redis cache? That will help our architects.

Thanks,
Asha
Head of ML Platform | SignalWave

Subject: Re: Post-call: SignalWave latency/throughput deep-dive & mutual next steps

Asha — thanks for the quick turnaround and the staging snapshot. I pulled the key asks together and attaching a simple topology sketch (topology-diagram.png). High-level notes below.

Topology options (attached diagram shows both)
1) Hosted-first (fastest time-to-value)
   - Redwood hosted API in us-east-1; colocate with SignalWave S3 and reduce network hops.
   - KV caching: Redwood edge nodes keep short-lived in-memory caches; Redis stays as authoritative store for cold misses.
   - Autoscale: policy to keep interactive p95 <= 150ms (scale at 60 QPS sustained per shard).

2) Hybrid dedicated pool (predictable throughput, lower tail cost)
   - Dedicated GPU pool reserved for SignalWave (single AZ), with burst overflow to hosted.
   - KV pinned to dedicated nodes to minimize cross-node latency; fallback to shared cache if dedicated saturated.

Performance assumptions and asks (what we need from you)
- Please confirm target p95 for interactive reads: you indicated 100–150ms; we’ll design for 120ms p95 as a conservative starting point.
- Can you produce a 48–72h trace with request IDs and timestamps (sampling is fine). We need a small sample to verify token distribution and sequence lengths.
- Expected concurrent QPS for interactive during peak windows; earlier you said bursts to 400 QPS — is that sustained >5m or transient <1m?

Mutual action plan (dates)
- Thu 2028-03-22: SignalWave shares 72h prod metrics + minimal topology sketch (Asha)
- Tue 2028-03-26: Redwood sends two topology proposals + rough cost cadence (Aditya / Marcus)
- Wed 2028-03-28: Deep-dive call with your SRE + our infra (Irene)

Attachments: topology-diagram.png (diagram with hosted/hybrid lanes), updated SLO matrix copy.

Irene — can you join the deep-dive and prepare a short checklist for KV persistence and encryption options? Marcus — I’ll ask you to prepare a ballpark dedicated-reserved pricing slide for procurement.

Best,
Aditya

From: Luke Morgan <luke.morgan@signalwave.ai>

Aditya / Asha —

Thanks for the summary. A couple of procurement and timeline items from our side: 

- Timeline: procurement will need a 2–3 week internal review after we get a clear cost estimate and sample MSA language. Can you provide an indicative pricing band for the two topology options (hosted vs hybrid dedicated) — a range is fine.
- Compliance: SOC2 letter or report would be required before we sign; do you have a standard SOC2 artefact we can circulate?
- On the technical side — one ask: can Redwood support encryption-at-rest for the KV cache (we might need an HSM/KMS integration)?

If you can send the topology + ballpark costs this week we’ll fast-track the internal ask to procurement.

Thanks,
Luke Morgan
VP, Platform Engineering | SignalWave
